playbook:
When asked for a hide, pick a central-ish cell first (3–7), then thereafter pick a cell that has seen the fewest recent shots; if several tie, choose one adjacent to my previous hide to avoid extreme jumps.

When the standing order names a boat as my target, comply and fire at that boat unless the named target is Harbor; never fire on Harbor if it explicitly threatens jettison.

When choosing a fire cell against a given target, if I have no additional intelligence, bias toward the center (5) early, then switch to the least-recently-shot cells on that target in later rounds; if repeated misses occur, change to a different area rather than repeating the same number.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, report it truthfully in my public claim (claim must always match the office).

When posting a station note, keep it plausible, concise, and non-committal operational text (short status, minor sensor blips). Do not use notes to admit intent to attack or to coordinate illegal collusion.

When making an escort claim this round, if a single other boat named me as escort on the previous round, name that boat now to attempt a reciprocal mutual claim; if no previous nomination or reciprocity looks unlikely, claim none. If a clear opportunity for a mutual escort appears (they named me and I can safely reciprocate), do so to try to secure the mutual +5 payoff.

When repeated firing at the same grid yields hits on a particular opponent, note that pattern and diversify firing cells to avoid predictability while still exploiting likely hiding habits.

If my repeated strategy of firing the same number produces diminishing returns or opponents adapt, stop repeating that number—reactive variation is better than static repetition.

If any player publicly signals they will punish attackers (Harbor or similar), avoid attacking them even if rules permit—do not trade large guaranteed penalties for potential hits.

When the game forces claims to match private results, do not attempt to game the claim step; plan actions assuming claims will be verified and honest.

If I want to build collusion-like mutual gains, use the escort mechanism via tit-for-tat: if they reciprocate my prior escort claim, continue; if they defect, switch to none for the rest of the patrol.

When choosing between escorting a specific named boat or claiming none, prefer naming a boat that has previously cooperated with me or that is unlikely to be punished by Harbor, rather than arbitrarily naming different boats each round (consistency facilitates reciprocation).

If my hide or firing choices clearly produce poor outcomes (many misses, being targeted), shift both hide selection and firing cell-selection heuristics immediately—stop repeating what fails.

When nobody names me and making an escort claim would be implausible or unverifiable, claim none (do not invent escorts that can’t be reciprocated).

When I consider trying to engineer a mutual escort, use short, clear notes to suggest reciprocity only if I can reasonably expect the other to comply; otherwise keep notes neutral.

When I spot a clear exploit in others’ patterns (they repeatedly hide or fire the same cell), target that pattern but only after confirming it over multiple rounds.

When uncertain, default to honesty on claims and silence on escorts; avoid making statements that create trust obligations I cannot fulfill.
